replication.target_description: Unresolved target within Replication Study 2 of original Study 4, p. 6 §5.2: GCBS and Belief in 7/7 conspiracy theories are separate independent-samples tests. Both assigned rows have identical neutral descriptions and locators. Description names scrambled sentences, whereas this study uses disfluent fonts.

reported_success.quote: Overall, similarly to Replication Study 1, the original study failed to ... replicate. We found no evidence that the analytical thinking primes ... lowered belief in conspiracy theories.

notes: Identity independently checked within the supplied canonical text: UvA repository cover and article title identify No evidence that priming analytic thinking reduces belief in conspiracy theories; authors Većkalov, Gligorić and Petrović; DOI 10.1016/j.jesp.2023.104549; JESP 110 (2024), 104549. Cover labels Final published version; text includes methods, results, discussion and references. This is the primary final replication report, not an abstract or preregistration. No PDF was supplied (source_pdf_path null). Original source and unassigned fields were not examined; nulls there are placeholders. Target ambiguity: Study 2 uses disfluent fonts, not the scrambled-sentence task in the supplied description. The p. 6 locator contains two conspiracy outcomes, and nothing supplied distinguishes audit rows 1985 and 1986. Candidate GCBS: d = 0.06, t(486) = 0.63, p = .529 (exact/equality), 95% CI [− 0.12, 0.25]. Candidate London 7/7: d = 0.11, t(486) = 1.27, p = .206 (exact/equality), 95% CI [− 0.07, 0.30]. No assignment by row order or numeric matching. Candidate common final participant N = 488 is explicitly printed after 19 quality exclusions from 507 completers; no speeders and no outliers in either DV, so no outlier reanalysis. N remains candidate-only pending field-scope review because target correspondence is unresolved. Reported failed replication is the authors’ explicit study-wide verdict and applies to both outcomes independently of unresolved coefficient selection.
